name: circling-elements

frames.best_why: The six photos are spread evenly around the ring, making the orbit obvious at a glance.

tagline: Six square photos drift around an empty centre, pausing under the cursor.
summary: Small square images spaced evenly on an invisible ring orbit a blank middle at a steady speed; hovering the group freezes the motion and each tile enlarges.
appearance: Six small square photos of a pug, blossom, dune, flower, snowy peak and a dark figure float in a loose circle on a black stage. Their spacing is even, the middle is empty, and there are no frames or labels around them.
behaviour: The set turns continuously around the centre at a constant rate. Resting the pointer anywhere on the group stops the orbit, and the hovered photo grows slightly; leaving resumes the spin.
demo_content: Six small photos: a pug, cherry blossom, sand dune, red flower, snowy peak and a dark figure.
use_when: A portfolio or gallery wants a playful, always-moving arrangement of thumbnails around a focal blank space.
avoid_when: Many images or precise browsing: the constant orbit and fixed radius make individual tiles awkward to target.
customise: Children are the orbiting items; radius, duration, easing, direction, pause-on-hover and class names are props, so each tile's size and hover style live in its own markup.
weight_why: Six small images each run one CSS keyframe; no JavaScript runs per frame.

a11y.note: The continuous orbit ignores prefers-reduced-motion, and the tiles are plain images with no controls.

issues: The orbit radius is fixed in pixels, so on narrow screens the outer tiles spill past the viewport.
polish_why: Simple and clear orbit with real photos; fixed radius and uneven gaps keep it ordinary.
title: Circling Elements
